videos.script: Before anybody screws an access point to a ceiling, somebody should know where it goes. {{ceiling}} Guessing is common. One access point for every so many square metres, in the middle of each room. It fails in ways a floor plan does not show. {{guess}} A concrete lift shaft can block more signal than thirty metres of open office. A coated glass wall looks transparent. It can block more than a brick one. {{walls}} A site survey replaces the guess with measurements. It comes in three kinds. A prediction made in software. A walk that listens to what is on the air. And a walk that connects, and measures what a user gets. {{kinds}} In this lesson you will compute how a signal falls with distance and with walls. {{formula}} You will meet the numbers a design is judged by. And you will find out why minus sixty-seven dBm keeps coming up. {{target}} Then you will read a heat map. It shows a great deal, and it hides some things that matter. {{heatmap}} The lab has no radio, so every number here is computed. The lesson says which ones are rules of thumb. {{computed}}
